newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel hopes to carry passengers next week.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel hopes to carry passengers next week.

text.p: The French co-chairman of Eurotunnel said on Wednesday he hoped passenger service through the fire-damaged Channel tunnel would resume early next week, but added full repairs would take three-to-five months.
"Our target is to re-establish Eurostar traffic and our tourist shuttles at the beginning of next week," Patrick Ponsolle told Europe 1 radio.

The tunnel has been closed to passenger traffic, including the Eurostar high-speed train service, since a fire on November 18 destroyed a freight train and severely damaged a 300 metre section of tunnel, injuring 34 people .
Partial freight traffic resumed on November 21.
Ponsolle said the resumption of passenger traffic through the tunnel depended on approval from safety authorities which Eurotunnel hoped to receive by the end of this week.
Investigators have determined no cause for the fire and Ponsolle said he was ruling out no possible causes -- including sabotage.
"That is the part of the event that remains mysterious," he said.

In a statement which could lift the spirits of battered shareholders in the debt-laden Franco-British company, Ponsolle said Eurotunnel would feel no financial impact from the fire because it had ample insurance coverage.
"We are under no financial pressure because we have insurance which covers our operating losses," Ponsolle told Europe 1 radio.
Ponsolle said the loss or earnings from the fire could be "significant" but did not give a figure.
The maximum coverage of Eurotunnel's insurance is 1.5 billion francs ($290 million) for equipment and 4.5 billion for earnings losses, Ponsolle said.
"We are covered by a very, very, very large margin," Ponsolle said.
He said the train which was destroyed in the fire was worth a little less than 100 million francs and that the repair work would cost between 200 million and 500 million francs.
Current restrictions to tunnel use are costing Eurotunnel about a million sterling in lost revenue each day.
Eurotunnel is awaiting the results of insurer investigations into the costs of the fire.
On Tuesday, French insurer Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP), one of Eurotunnel's lead insurers, said it was impossible to quantify the cost of the damage to the tunnel.
Eurotunnel is also facing possible legal action over lost earnings by companies operating the Eurostar and French and Belgian national railway systems.
